cards.title: First Response Is Back — Send One on Every Ticket
cards.bodyHtml:
Effective Now First response time is returning to our service metrics. Go back to sending a first response on tickets instead of waiting to reply in full — a macro for this is in the works.

Note: this reverses the earlier "reply FULLY, don't send a first-response-only" guidance in the Ticket Workflow & Expectations card below.

How to Triage Your First Response

Heavy-lift ticket (student removals, BatSignals, etc.): send a quick acknowledgment — "Thank you for reaching out to Varsity Tutors! My name is ____. Please allow me some time to complete your request for ____." — then move to the next ticket before committing to the longer one.

Needs more info (for example, which students to remove): ask your clarifying question and move on.

No real work needed (automatic email replies, etc.): reply fully and solve it right away.

Also: work your queue oldest to newest — sort by created date to keep things in order.

cards.title: Auto-Assign Is Live — CSO Ticketing & LLP
cards.bodyHtml:
Stop Manually Claiming Tickets Starting 9/22, CSO Ticketing tickets are auto-assigned — up to 15 Waiting for Support tickets per agent (Waiting on Tutor tickets don't count toward that max).

Keep Your Status Accurate Auto Assign routes based on your status. Keep it accurate all day long — work block, breaks, meals, and Offline at EOS — or Auto Assign will keep routing tickets to you even when you're not actually working.

Phase 2 Live — LLP Auto-Assign As of 9/29, LLP auto-assign is live as well. If you're on a CHAT+T block and a waiting LLP comes in, you no longer need to manually grab it from Live Support Requests — switch your status to LLP+T and the waiting LLP will be automatically assigned to you.

Note: the "claim tickets," "cherry-picking," and "check the queue for unclaimed tickets" guidance in the Ticket Workflow & Expectations card no longer applies — both ticket types are now auto-assigned.

cards.title: Team Update — Katie Has Left the Company
cards.bodyHtml: Katie Rosenhamer McCormick is no longer with the company. Megan remains everyone's point of contact for questions, concerns, or anything else you need.

cards.title: Daylight Saving Time Ends 11/1 — Check Your Local Start Time
cards.bodyHtml:
Daylight Saving Time ends in most of the US on Sunday, November 1, 2026 at 2:00 AM local time. Schedules are based on St. Louis, MO (Central Time) — your scheduled shift time in St. Louis time stays the same, but if your local time zone doesn't shift the same way, your local start time may change.

How to Check Use a time zone converter, set the date to November 2 (or your next shift after the change), enter your scheduled shift time in the St. Louis field, and check the corresponding time for your location.

Double-check your start times for shifts beginning Sunday, November 1st onward. Questions or help calculating your adjusted time — reach out to Misha or post in the scheduling channel.

cards.title: LOD Agent Status Management — New Feature
cards.bodyHtml:
LODs can now change your status directly when additional coverage is needed, primarily for LLP. You'll get an on-screen notification when this happens.

Do Not Switch Yourself Back If an LOD moves you to LLP+T, it means LLP volume is high and more coverage is needed. Stay available for LLP support until volume is under control — the LOD will switch you back to your previous status once it's no longer needed.

LODs can also use this feature to correct a status someone forgot to update for EOS, Break, or Meal.

cards.title: MA/NJ Tutor Contract Reduction — New Required Macros
cards.bodyHtml:
We're reducing the number of tutors contracted in Massachusetts (MA) and New Jersey (NJ). New macros have been added to the Admin Hub for this.

The Short Version

Tutors can work out their current contract if they have active students.

Tutors in MA/NJ will no longer receive new students or opportunities.

Tutors with an address in these states cannot reactivate.

Update the Macro to Match Their State You must update the macro to reflect the tutor's correct state — the pink banner may or may not appear, so review the account carefully either way. This works the same as our existing no-contract states; these are just the required macros for MA/NJ specifically.

Take the confirmation quiz to confirm you've read and understand this change (link shared in Slack).

cards.title: Platform Support: Outbound Call Expectations
cards.bodyHtml:
Before placing an outbound call to a client, check with the LOD on shift to make sure there's enough coverage for live LLP requests.

The Process

Check with your LOD before calling — they'll review LLP volume and coverage to approve or hold off.

Once approved, place the call and troubleshoot the issue.

If the call approaches 15 minutes without a resolution, offer to escalate to Tier 3.

If the client or tutor asks for a specific callback time, explain we can't guarantee that exact time — if it's their only option, escalate to Tier 3 instead.

A broad availability window (for example, "anytime before 5pm EST") is not a reason to escalate — coordinate with your LOD and call within that window; no need to follow up to pin down an exact time.

Non-Negotiable Always change your status to SBO when placing an outbound call, and always add the FLEX call link to the ticket to document the interaction.

cards.title: Status Timing — No Early Breaks/Meals, Report Auto-Assign Issues
cards.bodyHtml:
Don't move into break or meal status early — the only exception is End of Shift (EOS). This has always been the rule, including for closers: if you're closing shift, log off exactly when your shift ends rather than going offline early.

Report Auto-Assign Problems Immediately If something isn't working — like LLP Auto-Assign not routing tickets to you during a scheduled coverage window — report it right away rather than letting it go unnoticed. Repeated unreported issues will start being tracked as a behavioral concern.

cards.title: New Ticket Notification Badges — Coming Soon
cards.bodyHtml:
A new feature is coming to Tutor Admin to help you stay on top of tickets needing attention, visible throughout Tutor Admin:

Waiting for Support badge — shows how many tickets are waiting on an agent response.

URGENT badge — flags high-priority tickets, especially from ClientHUD.

Treat Urgent as Urgent URGENT tickets should be a "drop what you're doing" situation — they should never sit in the queue while lower-priority tickets get worked first.

We'll share another update once this is released.

cards.title: New Tutor Experience Rolling Out
cards.bodyHtml: A new tutor experience is rolling out — things may be in different places compared to the old one. When a tutor needs help finding something on their dashboard, try impersonating them to see the new layout and guide them accurately.

cards.title: New LLP2 Layout & Features (Including Doodle)
cards.bodyHtml: A new LLP2 layout and set of functions, including Doodle, is rolling out shortly. Keep an eye out for spikes in issues or anything breaking and report what you see.

cards.title: Whiteboard Not Connecting — Brazil ISP Issue
cards.bodyHtml: Some internet providers in Brazil are blocking the connection to the whiteboard, affecting students or LLP agents in Brazil. Workaround: use a VPN set to the US or another country to resolve the connection issue.

cards.title: Client Assessment Popup Blocking Homepage — Known Issue
cards.bodyHtml: Some clients are reaching out because an assessment is popping up instead of their usual homepage. This is being escalated. For now, have them complete the assessment so they can get into their profile — one workaround that seems to help permanently is entering all student info, then selecting "Not right now" when asked about adding 1:1 tutoring.

cards.title: Merge Tickets Carefully — Read the Tutor's Request First
cards.bodyHtml: Before merging tickets, make sure you've actually read the tutor's request on each one. A tutor may have another open ticket that isn't the same issue — merging unrelated tickets can bury a separate request.

cards.title: Exclusive Opportunity Issues — Who to Tag
cards.bodyHtml: If a tutor reaches out because they can't accept an exclusive opportunity, or a student wasn't assigned after they accepted, tag Camila Cardoso or Bianca Krutzsch in #transferchat. Only tag Bianca on Fridays and Saturdays.

cards.title: Urgent LLP Status Flip from Platform Support Tickets — Not a Bug
cards.bodyHtml:
Some Platform Support tickets can come in as an Urgent LLP and automatically flip your status to Busy, even though there's no actual live session. This happens because tutors can reach out to Platform Support about a session issue through Messages outside of the session itself — it's expected system behavior, not a bug.

What to Do Review the urgent ticket to see if anything needs immediate action, like joining a session or calling the tutor. If nothing's needed, manually switch your status back to LLP+T.

cards.title: Service Metrics Timer — No Hold Status, Timer Doesn't Pause for Busy/LLP
cards.bodyHtml:
Clarifying two recurring questions about how service metrics work:

Timer and Agent Status The timer does not run while a ticket is in Waiting on Tutor — it starts (or continues) once the tutor replies and the ticket moves to Waiting on Support. Whether you're Available, Busy, or actively on an LLP doesn't change the fact that the tutor is waiting — the metric reflects the tutor's experience, not agent availability.

No Hold Status We will not be adding a Hold status like Zendesk had. Zendesk didn't give us the flexibility to remove that option, which is why it was never meant to be used in the first place. Adding one here would let the clock pause while the tutor is still waiting, which defeats the purpose of the metric.

cards.title: Individual Agent Queues Live in Tutor Admin
cards.bodyHtml: Your name now appears under CSO Ticketing with your own individual queue, showing just the tickets assigned to you. CSO Ticketing still remains the team's main queue for looking up other tickets or reviewing waiting LLPs.

cards.title: Invoicing Admin Deprecated — Use Tutor Admin Instead
cards.bodyHtml: The old invoicing admin was quietly deprecated back in July. The current go-to page for invoices is now in Tutor Admin: varsitytutors.com/tutor-admin/invoicing.

cards.title: Okta MFA — Enable Now to Avoid Lockout
cards.bodyHtml:
Action Required Okta Verify or Google Authenticator should be enabled as your Okta MFA — SMS is no longer offered as an MFA method, and anyone who hasn't switched over risks being locked out of Okta entirely.

Setup Instructions Okta Verify Setup Guide → | Google Authenticator Setup Guide →

Already Locked Out? Submit an IT ticket or post in #support-it-all-employees — IT will reset your MFA so you can set up Okta Verify or Google Authenticator at your next login.

Questions or issues: post in #support-it-all-employees or submit an IT ticket through the IT Service Desk.

cards.title: Payroll Support Moving to HR Jira Help Desk
cards.bodyHtml:
As of 9/25, all payroll questions go through the HR Jira Help Desk using the Payroll ticket type — not email.

Email Transition Emails to payroll@varsitytutors.com will auto-create a ticket, and all replies will come through Jira, not email. Internal emails to payroll@ will keep working through 10/25 — after that they'll bounce with instructions to submit a ticket instead.

Bookmark the link below and use it for all payroll requests going forward so nothing gets lost and you can track yours from start to finish.

New Link Payroll Help Desk →

cards.title: Waiting on Tutor — 24-Hour Manual-Solve Threshold
cards.bodyHtml:
Email tickets sitting in Waiting on Tutor for more than 24 hours with no response from the tutor can be solved directly — add an internal note (for example: "Ticket solved after more than 24 hours with no response from tutor") and solve it.

Not the Same as the 5-Day Auto-Close This is different from the system's automatic Closed-after-Solved timer (see the "Closed vs. Solved" card below). The 24 hours here is when you can proactively solve a stale Waiting on Tutor ticket yourself; the 5 days is how long a Solved ticket sits before the system moves it to Closed on its own.

cards.title: ClientHUD & Client Tickets — Full Update
cards.bodyHtml:
Public Reply works directly on ClientHUD tickets — you can respond to the client straight from the ticket. We can also now create real tickets for clients: in Create Ticket, switch the Tutor/Client toggle to Client, enter their email, and write your message — attachments and screenshots work too.

Copy the Email Carefully The system doesn't validate the client's email yet, so copy/paste it directly from VTWA or ClientHUD rather than typing it.

Missing Client Email — Mostly Resolved The bug causing missing client emails on ClientHUD BatSignal tickets has been fixed — new tickets should come in with the email attached. If you still see one missing, report it with the ticket link.

If You Still Hit a Missing Email Don't send a BatSignal or canned email. Use Create Ticket to make a real client ticket instead, and merge the original ClientHUD ticket into it if you can. If merge isn't working, link the new ticket in internal notes and solve the original — either way, add a Public Reply to the original referencing the new ticket before solving it, so your metrics reflect a response.

Tier 3 Client Tickets — Workaround Retired Since client ticket creation is fully working, we no longer use the test tutor account for Tier 3 client tickets. Create them directly using the Client toggle. The SOP has been updated to reflect this — if Tier 3 receives one created the old way, they'll send it back to be resubmitted correctly.

We still can't reply through LLP Client chat — the client's account doesn't receive those messages, so nothing sent there is visible to them.

cards.title: Overlapping/Multiple First-Session Bookings — Known Bug
cards.bodyHtml:
Engineering is aware of an issue where tutors submit more than one option for a first session and all of them get scheduled. A ticket has been filed; no ETA yet.

What to Do

Double-check whether the tutor has confirmed the intended session time with the client — encourage them to reach out if they haven't.

If the client isn't responding, remove all sessions except the one that's actually wanted.

Let the tutor know this is a known, reported issue.

If a client gets charged for one of the extra sessions, report it right away.

cards.title: Closed vs. Solved — Don't Manually Close Tickets
cards.bodyHtml: Reminder Do not set tickets to Closed after responding to the tutor. All tickets should be set to Solved only — the system will move it to Closed automatically after 5 days. We've had feedback from tutors that their tickets were being closed immediately and they couldn't submit follow-up questions.

cards.title: Tier 3 Escalation — Follow the Full SOP + New Macro
cards.bodyHtml:
Follow the Full Process Please make sure to follow the Tier 3 SOP when escalating tickets to the T3 queue — several recent tickets have skipped Step 2 for tutor escalations.

When creating the new Tier 3 ticket, first send this as a public reply to the tutor: "Hello, this is to confirm that I've forwarded your issue to our Tier 3 team. You will be contacted within 24 hours through this new ticket."

Once the ticket is created and the public reply sent, add all troubleshooting details, findings, and additional info as internal notes.

New Macro Use the "Tier 3 first response" macro to send that public reply (tutor-facing only for now).

If you need a refresher, the SOP is on the KB: fellowship-kb.netlify.app/a/gen-012

cards.title: Auto-QA Is Back
cards.bodyHtml:
Auto-QA has returned and scoring has resumed as normal.

Disagree With a Score? Leave a comment on your scorecard — the LLM can make mistakes, so flag anything that looks off.

cards.title: Work Block Priority Change — CHAT+T vs LLP+T
cards.bodyHtml:
Immediate Change — Please Acknowledge Effective immediately, we're changing work block priorities:

If your work block shows LLP+T, your primary focus is LLP. In between LLP/PS requests, you can work TES tickets. If you're working a TES ticket and an LLP comes in, claim the LLP immediately — no exceptions.

If your work block shows CHAT+T, your primary focus is now TES tickets. Only step in to assist with LLPs if we're backed up and additional support is needed.

LOD: use @everyone in the Health channel only if all primary LLP agents are already tied up with LLPs and additional support is needed. A message sent without @everyone is meant for the agents currently assigned to LLP.

cards.title: TQI Verification Step Added — First Session Reschedule/Cancel SOP
cards.bodyHtml:
Effective Immediately Tutors changing or canceling a first session through the mobile app can be redirected correctly, have a ticket open, and still get hit with a TQI. We're not yet sure if the web experience is also affected — still validating.

New Step Before proceeding on any first-session reschedule/cancel ticket, verify whether a TQI has already been applied, regardless of where the tutor's message came in. If one has, follow the escalation process to have it removed when appropriate.

TQIs should ONLY be removed if the tutor backs out of their request, the client requested the change, or the tutor stops responding.

cards.title: First Session Reschedule/Cancel Tickets — Solving Too Early Will Fail QA
cards.bodyHtml:
We're auditing team tickets and found a concerning trend: First Session Reschedule/Cancel tickets are being marked Solved right after our first reply, even when a response from the tutor is mandatory.

No Rule Change — Enforcement Change Tickets automatically close after 24 hours. You should not solve a ticket unless no response from the tutor is needed, or a Senior/Lead has instructed otherwise. If we're genuinely waiting on the tutor, use the Waiting on Tutor status. Going forward, tickets solved this way will be manually pulled into QA and failed.

cards.title: Reassigned-to-Former-Student Rate Handling — Do Not Alter Rates
cards.bodyHtml:
Effective Immediately — Absolutely No Exceptions Do not manually change base rates for tutors who are reassigned to a former student.

Incentive Progress Now Carries Over Automatically For eligible incentive programs, a tutor reconnecting with a recent student within 90 days now has their incentive progress continue automatically instead of restarting. We are no longer manually updating base rates for this — no exceptions.

Verbiage for tutors: "If your student was eligible for incentives before they were deactivated, the incentives will resume automatically but may not be reflected in your base rate. We are no longer manually updating base rates and we appreciate your understanding. If you believe the incentives are not applying, please reach out to our Disbursements Team at payments@varsitytutors.com and they will be able to look into this for you."

Exception — V1 Incentives

For V1 incentives (applied before the V2 update), manual rate restoration is still allowed, but double-check first — confirm the base rate actually changed in VTWA, usually by checking the date of the student's initial assignment. If a rate wasn't restored properly on reinstatement within 90 days, flag the example to Engineering — send it in the work channel and tag Ramon or Austin.

cards.title: VT4S Wind-Down — Macros Live
cards.bodyHtml:
Action Required Nerdy is winding down the VT4S (K-12) school/district business to focus on the consumer-facing tutoring business. Macros to handle related questions are now live:

There's one for tutors, addressing the end of VT4S opportunities.

There's a SEPARATE macro for clients if we get a login issue on a VT4S account — it redirects to our website at the end. If the client starts asking about plans or pricing, send them the sales phone number on our main webpage and let them know sales will help from there.

Double-Check Before Sending Take a beat and make sure you've picked the correct macro before sending.

Note: one-to-one, consumer-facing tutoring is not impacted by this change — tutors under contract with Varsity Tutors LLC remain under contract for those opportunities.

cards.title: Admin Hub Ticket Queue Cleanup — Timeout Fix
cards.bodyHtml:
The ticket queue view now defaults to showing only Unclaimed, Waiting on Support, and Waiting on Tutor tickets. This also fixes the timeout errors people were seeing in Admin Hub. Refresh Admin Hub to see the change.

Feedback Wanted This was a big ask from the team — please make sure to update and leave feedback on how the new queue view is working for you.

cards.title: Nerdy Assistant Chrome Extension — Mandatory Rollout
cards.bodyHtml:
Action Required A new tool, the Nerdy Assistant Chrome Extension, is rolling out to the whole team — designed to cut handle time and help us work tickets and LLPs faster. It will be available starting Monday, with the possibility of earlier access. Using it will be mandatory for everyone as soon as it becomes available.

A quick guide covering setup, functionality, and goals for the tool has been shared: Nerdy Assistant Quick Guide. Questions about the guide can go to Joao directly; questions about the tool can go here, in the work channel, or to your Senior.

Known Issue The Ask Anything / knowledge-search function is currently referencing a deprecated Knowledge Base. Double-check its answers thoroughly until this is addressed — the information it returns can be outdated.

cards.title: Tutor IDs — Uploads Only, No Email/Ticket Submissions
cards.bodyHtml: Tutors are no longer allowed to submit IDs to us through email or a ticket. They must upload the ID directly through their profile using the ID verification process. If they're having trouble with that, send them to Recruitment and explain that the tutor is unable to upload their ID.

cards.title: Agent Statuses — Start Using Them
cards.bodyHtml:
Start using the agent statuses now — they don't drive anything yet, but get in the habit. An LoD status will be added shortly.

Status Dropdown Updated "Available" has been removed from the status dropdown. Use CHAT+T or LLP+T depending on your scheduled work block (see the Work Block Priority Change card). There's also a Busy status — do not select it for any reason — and a Tier 3 status for scheduled Tier 3 blocks.

Two Quick Tips Don't close Admin Index when you step away for lunch — it will boot your status offline. Mute the tab if you don't want to hear the notification sound, and unmute when you're back.

A fix has been deployed for the bug where refreshing or re-entering the URL could drop your status to offline. Keep flagging it in the team channel if you still see it happening.

cards.title: Time Off & Call Outs — Paylocity Only
cards.bodyHtml:
Scheduled time off requests should be entered in Paylocity. Call outs should be submitted through the Assembled workflow — and you must also drop a message to a lead or to Katie if you're calling out.

Full-Time Schedules Have Resumed We're back to normal full-time schedules. VTO/MTO will be very limited, if offered at all — please don't rely on it; if you need time off, schedule it. If you have a Platform Support block, LLP calls are still priority during that block — pause other ticket work to take them.
Resubmit If Needed Any time off that was approved before we moved into Paylocity must be resubmitted in Paylocity ASAP — no exceptions.

Scheduled time off requests are now being reviewed 30 days out (example: October requests are reviewed in September, November requests in October).

cards.title: QA Reviews & 1:1s — Don't Wait
cards.bodyHtml: 1:1s are being scheduled. Review your QAs in a timely manner — scores from several weeks back will not be adjusted.

cards.title: Reschedule Friction SOP — Rollout Complete
cards.bodyHtml:
Rollout Recap Additional friction was introduced for tutors attempting to reschedule their first session with a new student. The rollout started at 25% (7/28) and expanded to 500 tutors by end of week.

Reference The SOP is documented here: Reschedule Friction SOP. The mandatory acknowledgment form has closed — no further action needed unless you were told otherwise directly.

cards.title: Session Lookup — New Admin Hub Tool
cards.bodyHtml:
There's a new Session Lookup tool in the Admin Hub (Insights → Quality → Session Lookup) that lets you review session details without needing the #session-verification channel.

To search, you'll need the Tutor ID, Client ID, and session date — you do not need the Session UID.

Known Limitation If the tutor didn't select "End the session for everyone," the "Ended at" time may not appear. If there's no "Ended at" info available, use #session-verification for further review.

cards.title: QA Scorecards — View Previous Week
cards.bodyHtml: You can now view the previous week's scorecards on your QA.

cards.title: Member Services — Transfer Opportunity
cards.bodyHtml: Check your email for a message about an opportunity to transfer into Member Services. One of the available roles includes a monthly bonus opportunity, and there may also be opportunities for extra hours (not guaranteed). Reach out with questions.

cards.title: LLP Handle Time — Action Needed
cards.bodyHtml:
We've been reviewing LLP handle time over the past few weeks and have seen a significant increase, even though overall ticket volume is lower. Our average LLP handle time has climbed well beyond our 15-minute goal, and we need to correct this before the busy season begins.

Biggest Contributors

Do not send a first response before joining the session — claim the ticket and join immediately, this is no longer optional

Take control of the interaction and lead the troubleshooting: Join → Troubleshoot → Resolve → Exit

Do not assist with Tutor Support issues during an LLP — if a tutor has scheduling, invoice, or other non-technical questions, direct them to Tutor Support

Close your tickets promptly — leaving a ticket open after you've exited the LLP still counts against your handle time. Workflow: Claim → Join → Troubleshoot → Wrap up the ticket → Mark as Solved

Watch the Clock Keep an eye on the 15-minute goal for every LLP interaction. If you're approaching that mark and the issue is still unresolved, start looking for a workaround and consider recommending Tier 3.

cards.title: Team Homepage Has a New Home
cards.bodyHtml:
The Team Homepage has moved — please bookmark the new link below.

New Link Team Homepage

For now, ignore the Team Hub — it's out of date and being reworked; an update is coming.

cards.title: Ticket Workflow & Expectations
cards.bodyHtml:
Where and How We Work

Work out of the CSO Ticketing tab. All Platform Support and Tutor Support tickets are grouped here.

See Auto-Assign Card Above CSO Ticketing tickets are now auto-assigned instead of manually claimed — see the "Auto-Assign Is Live" card at the top of this page. The claiming guidance just below now applies to Live Requests only.

Claim the next available ticket and work tickets in the order they come in. Cherry-picking is not permitted. Claim one or two tickets at a time — five at most, and that should not be often. Solve or answer a ticket, check the queue for new unclaimed tickets, and repeat.

LLP Is the Exception LLP takes priority. Pause your email and chat tickets to accept a live LLP session as quickly as possible. >> UPDATE << Cross-training on Platform Support and LLP is now complete for all agents — we operate as one team, with no more "TES agents" vs. "LLP agents" split. If an LLP comes in and you're not actively troubleshooting another LLP session, claim it. No exceptions. Once LLP demand is covered, return to working tickets.

Expectations

Work a minimum of 75 tickets per week (seasonal adjustment).

Handle times should be 5 minutes or less for non-live work. Handle times are now tracked.

Take a fair share of both Platform Support and Tutor Support — do not avoid one queue.

See First Response Card Above First response time is back in our metrics — see the "First Response Is Back" card at the top of this page.

Daily Workflow Reminders << Check for unclaimed tickets → send a first response → review any Waiting on Support tickets in your queue → reply → check for unclaimed tickets again

Watch your handle time — use the clock. If you have too many tabs open, close a few; if you get distracted mid-ticket, try an external timer to remind you to check back

Work oldest to newest

Track Yourself

You can track your own progress on the Leaderboard in the Admin Hub, under the Support tab. It defaults to Week to Date. To see today, set a custom date range with today's date as the start and end, and filter by your name. Your metrics aren't hidden from you — use them to prepare for your 1:1s.

cards.title: We No Longer Work in a Chat Environment
cards.bodyHtml:
Reminder When a tutor reaches out through their Tutor Profile, the interaction may look like a chat because it appears under their Messages — but on our end, it is a ticket and must be handled as one.

Do not use old chat macros (for example, "It's been a few minutes since I've received a response, so this chat will be disconnected.") — we are not disconnecting a chat. Send your response and manage the ticket using the appropriate status.

Do not move a ticket directly to Closed and skip Solved. This is not allowed unless a Sr. Agent or Lead specifically instructs you to do so — macros that are built to auto-close (like the reactivation-declined macro) are the one exception and are fine as-is.

Tickets must follow the correct workflow and status progression.

Heads Up Either of the above issues may result in the QA being placed into a FAIL state.

cards.title: Reclassify Technical Tickets → Platform Support
cards.bodyHtml: Some Platform Support issues arrive in the Tutor Support queue. Reclassify these so your Platform Support work is counted correctly — change the support group from Tutor Support to Platform Support. Common examples: email changes, password resets, error messages on the tutor experience, Inova lockouts, and any technical troubleshooting related to platform access or functionality. When in doubt, ask in the team channel before changing it.

cards.title: Team Knowledge Base Is Live
cards.bodyHtml:
We now have a team knowledge base with 95 articles, all updated recently for accuracy. It now includes all the content that used to live in our playbooks, with recent SOPs still being added — so be patient if something is missing. »» The KB has moved to Netlify — bookmark the new link below.

New Link Knowledge Base → (https://fellowship-kb.netlify.app/)

cards.title: Using Claude — Verify Before You Use It
cards.bodyHtml:
When you get information from Claude, double-check it before you rely on it.

Do Not Do not share internal information with the tutor, and do not copy and paste Claude's exact words into an email thread.

We are still learning how it gathers information, so the safest option is to use our own resources and check with a colleague, Senior, or Lead.

cards.title: Bug: Graduate Test Prep Rate Defaulting to $18
cards.bodyHtml: There is a bug where the graduate test prep rate type is defaulting to $18. Workaround: adjust the rate on the student side to the correct rate.

cards.title: Grabbing a Ticket Resets the Handle Time
cards.bodyHtml: If you take a ticket from another agent, you do not inherit the time already spent on it. The clock starts from zero as soon as another agent claims it. This is a fix for a known problem and is rolling out through the system.

cards.title: ClientHud — Reviewing a Client's Past Interactions
cards.bodyHtml: In ClientHud you can review a client's previous interactions. Search by the client ID (it is included in the ticket's internal notes). Open the account, scroll to the Recent Contacts section, and make sure the Support tab is selected. Click any interaction to review the details. You will also have access to the associated ZD tickets.

cards.title: New Client Experience — Take a Look
cards.bodyHtml: A new client experience has rolled out. If you have an account, log in and take some time to familiarize yourself with it.

cards.title: Escalated Reports — "Reports 2026" Tab
cards.bodyHtml: The MASTER Tickets spreadsheet has a new tab called "Reports 2026" with the issues we've escalated. Tracking started about a month ago, so it covers the most recent reports rather than everything. View the MASTER Tickets Spreadsheet →

cards.title: Always Leave an Internal Note
cards.bodyHtml:
Every ticket needs an internal note — even a one-line summary of what happened. Documentation is the most heavily weighted QA category, and a ticket with no internal note is an automatic fail no matter how good the rest of the interaction was.

When You Attach a Screenshot Type the word "screenshot" in your note (for example: "screenshot attached — confirmed 24HC request"). Attached images do not come through when tickets are exported for QA, so a note that is only a screenshot shows up blank and you lose credit.

cards.title: Reporting Admin Hub Issues → #tutor-admin-hub-ops-issues
cards.bodyHtml:
Report Admin Hub problems in #tutor-admin-hub-ops-issues. Keep reporting issues even if it is the same one several times a day — more reports help show impact and get fixes prioritized. This channel is also where you can post nice-to-have feature requests.

If You Record an Issue Use Loom, capture the entire screen (no cropped or single-tab recordings), and keep the browser console open and visible while you record.

cards.title: 24-Hour Cancellation Invoices
cards.bodyHtml:
How Auto-Invoicing Decides

The system decides what to invoice based on who cancels the session:

If a tutor cancels → no invoice is generated.

If a client cancels → a 24-hour cancellation invoice is generated.

If a tutor joins and no student is present → a no-show invoice is generated.

Manual 24HC — Proof Required We only enter a 24HC invoice manually when the tutor provides proof the client requested the cancellation. Proof must include the client name, contact info we can match to their account, the session date/time, and the time/date of cancellation (if not visible in VT Messages). Invoice these as an "unscheduled session." No proof = no invoice.

Advise tutors: if a client wants to cancel, the client must cancel from their end to avoid invoice processing delays.

Reschedules Within 24 Hours If a client reschedules a session within 24 hours of the start time, the tutor is no longer eligible for a 24HC invoice. We will not submit one, and one will not auto-generate. No exceptions.

No-show invoices are for the scheduled duration of the session. Tutors will eventually have a button to decline invoicing a client for a no-show or 24HC — no ETA on that feature yet.

Invoice Adjustments SOP A full breakdown of which invoice adjustments are and are not allowed is documented. View Invoice Adjustments SOP →

cards.bodyHtml: Report VT4S session problems — including session access 400 errors — in #llp-2-issues so they can be tracked and escalated.

cards.title: Tutor Resignations — How We Process Them
cards.bodyHtml:
The Tutor Requested macro has been added — it populates the instructions you need when submitting a resignation and will route the ticket to the appropriate team. Send the tutor the resignation verbiage first, before you use the Tutor Requested macro.

Flagging a Tutor for ANR Use the ANR Review macro (it replaces the old "ANR Found") to alert us of a tutor who may qualify for ANR. It routes to the Tutor Resignation queue.

To preserve our ticket count for these tickets, create a separate ticket to submit to the Tutor Resignations queue (with all the Tutor Requested macro steps included in the notes) instead of submitting the tutor's original ticket directly. This lets you Solve the original ticket so it counts toward metrics. Link the original ticket in the notes of the new one, and the new ticket in the notes of the original one.

cards.title: No-Show & Session Rules
cards.bodyHtml:
Wait Time

LLP shows tutors in-session messaging about auto-invoicing in real time. The wait time for a no-show is 10 minutes, not 15.

No Exceptions If the tutor leaves before the full 10 minutes, they are not paid the full hour for the no-show. No adjustments.

No-show invoices are for the scheduled duration of the session.

Instant Sessions

If a tutor reaches out about a no-show for an Instant Session where the student never joined, generate an invoice for 15 minutes only. Tutors should be compensated for their time.

Unconfirmed Sessions

Unconfirmed sessions no longer qualify for No-Show invoices. Still advise tutors to join unconfirmed sessions and wait the full window — the session may confirm, and it's the safer move either way. Tutors are not contractually obligated to join, but this makes everyone's lives easier.

Update — No-Show No Longer Applies Unconfirmed sessions no longer qualify for a No-Show invoice. Do not process a No-Show invoice for an unconfirmed session. This is a recent change — we'll update this section again if anything shifts.

VT4S Sessions

Tutors must stay for the entire duration of a VT4S session and bill normally, even if no students are present. The 15-minute rule does NOT apply to VT4S — except Parent-Led, which is allowed the 15-minute rule.

Background

The join link refresh remains rolled back — it interfered with the tutor's in-session time reading accurately for auto-invoicing. No ETA on re-enabling.

cards.title: Invoicing Update — Early Join Billable Time
cards.bodyHtml:
New Rule If both the tutor and student join before the scheduled start time, the system will pay for the early time — up to a maximum of 15 minutes.

Watch For The 15-minute early credit only applies when both the tutor and the student join early. If the tutor joins early (say, 30 minutes) but the student joins on time or late, the tutor's solo waiting time before the scheduled start is not billable.

cards.title: Tutor Replacement / Student Removal → Retention
cards.bodyHtml:
Regular (non-VT4S) student removals and tutor replacements go to Retention via BatSignal in the Admin Hub — do not post in #transferchat.

Required Include BOTH the tutor and client URLs in the body of the BatSignal ticket. Replacements have been delayed when one or both are missing.

All VT4S removals and drops use the VT4S escalation form instead — not BatSignal. Review the student removal process (KB article SYS-003): View Tutor Replacement Instructions →

cards.title: Group Courses & VT4S — Routing and Invoicing
cards.bodyHtml:
Routing

You can assign tickets to the Courses team in the Admin Hub for group or course issues that are outside our scope.

UPDATE (10/6) — We Now Handle Group Tutoring Tickets Now that we've completed training, we handle group tutoring tickets ourselves instead of routing them away. Group tutoring tickets appear in CSO Ticketing and do allow subs — check the group tutoring queue regularly to make sure nothing assigned to you goes unworked.

Invoicing Is Still Manual

Do Not Escalate to Disbursements Both Group Courses and VT4S are still on manual invoicing. Do not send invoice requests for either to Disbursements.

Group Courses: add the tutor back, have them submit the invoice, then unassign the course as soon as they submit. You may need to leave the ticket in Waiting on Tutor and follow up. VT4S: add the student back, submit the invoice on the tutor's behalf, then remove the student right away. All other auto-invoicing lines follow the standard escalation path to Disbursements when needed.

cards.title: Platform Support — Email Clients from VTWA
cards.bodyHtml: You do not have to call clients with updates on Platform Support tickets. You can email them from VTWA and the replies will come back to you. From the ticket: click the From: line, scroll up, choose techsupport@, then choose the blank template and compose your message. Replies arrive in the Admin Hub. This may create a new ticket that you will need to merge.

cards.title: LLP Get Help — Comes as a Ticket
cards.bodyHtml:
LLP Get Help no longer routes through a chat bot. Requests come in as tickets.

Important Any reply you send goes to the tutor's profile Messages — they won't see it during their session. Do not reply. Your immediate action is to join the session.

cards.title: Creating Tickets for Other Teams
cards.bodyHtml:
When creating a ticket to route to another team, include these required fields:

Subject: what the tutor requested.

Tutor UUID or Tutor ID: the number at the end of the tutor's VTWA URL.

Assigned team: the team the ticket needs to be assigned to.

Initial public message: a brief description for the tutor about the request being opened.

Critical Do not include internal information in the public message — it is visible to the tutor. Add internal notes after the ticket is created.

cards.title: Sending Working Links via Inline Code
cards.bodyHtml: Links pasted plainly in the Admin Hub may break on the tutor's end — in some cases a trailing ">" character is appended, returning a 404. Workaround: use the Inline Code feature to format the link before sending. This preserves the URL correctly. Alternative: send via canned response on the tutor's VTWA.

cards.title: Email Signatures — Manual Add Required
cards.bodyHtml: The Admin Hub does not auto-add your signature to emails. Add your signature manually to each reply.

cards.title: Subject Updates → Sourcing & Onboarding
cards.bodyHtml: Subject updates and subject assessment questions should be transferred to Sourcing & Onboarding via the Admin Hub. Do not post in #transferchat for these.

cards.title: Zero Opportunities — Subject Opt-In Prompt
cards.bodyHtml: Tutors with 0 opportunities and an Active-Meeting status will now be prompted to opt into subjects they are pre-approved for, or to complete interviews for related subjects. This is optional for the tutor, but it may help increase the number of opportunities they receive.

cards.title: Tutor Opportunity Notifications — Daily Digest Change
cards.bodyHtml:
What Changed

Tutors used to get an in-app notification, SMS, and email for every non-instant opportunity. That no longer happens — non-instant opportunities now go out in the Daily Digest email only, twice a day. The digest shows a count of available opportunities (not a list) and points tutors to the Tutor Dashboard. Still real-time and unchanged: instant requests, exclusive opportunities, and session reminders.

When the Digest Sends

Morning: 7:00 AM ET / 6:00 AM CT / 5:00 AM MT / 4:00 AM PT

Afternoon: 3:00 PM ET / 2:00 PM CT / 1:00 PM MT / 12:00 PM PT

Max two emails per day. Send times are fixed and don't shift to the tutor's local morning — that's why West Coast tutors get theirs at 4:00 AM and often miss it.

Two Things to Know The morning digest goes out to every eligible tutor even when there are zero opportunities. The afternoon digest only sends if new opportunities appeared since the morning — a missing afternoon email is normal and should not be escalated.

How to Investigate

Ask the tutor to check for the digest email from yesterday and this morning at the times above (check spam/junk too) — get a specific date.

If they received it: not a delivery issue — educate on the change.

If they received nothing: check notification preferences on their profile. If Daily Digest is off, that's the answer — re-enable and explain.

If Daily Digest is on and they still got nothing, report it so we can look into it.

cards.title: Invite-A-Friend on LLP2
cards.bodyHtml:
Now Live Students can invite a friend to join their session as a guest. 1:1 tutoring sessions only — not group sessions or VT4S.

How It Works

Only the student can invite — tutors do not have an invite button.

Student clicks Invite → tutor receives a yes/no approval prompt.

Once approved, the student can share or email a link to their friend.

The guest sees a Terms of Use screen before joining.

What to Expect

The client team will remind students to give their tutor a heads-up before the session. However, not all students will do this. Be ready for tutors asking for additional pay or wanting to drop students as a result of unexpected guests joining sessions.

cards.title: New Feature: Guaranteed Availability
cards.bodyHtml:
Rolling Out to 5% of Tutors Guaranteed Availability lets tutors mark specific time slots as open for instant student booking — no tutor approval required. Sessions are automatically confirmed. Tutors with GA slots are shown first in the Tutor Gallery.

Key rules to know:

Students must book at least 24 hours in advance

Booking window is limited to 8 days from today

Tutors can edit or remove unbooked slots at any time

Once a student books, the standard cancellation policy applies

Tutors can also mark time as Busy to block off personal time

View the full Guaranteed Availability FAQ →

Escalation Guidance Availability not showing in Tutor Gallery: Verify the tutor has a profile picture, Personal Statement, and signed ICAs in Account Settings. Student can't book an available slot: Confirm the session is more than 24 hours away and within the 8-day window. Tutor needs to cancel a booked GA session: Standard tutor cancellation policy applies.
